summary: Kyoshun Todo worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

Kyotaro Nishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Keio University from around 1949 to 1953 and served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties circa 1990 to 1996.

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Zuiryō-ji under Joten Soko Miura (~1928–1948). He served as abbot at Yotoku-in, Shojuan, and the Mount Baldy Zen Center, which he founded.

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Kyozo Yamada studied at the First Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University. A student of Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and other teachers, he founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai and became head of Sanbo Zen in 1970.

Kōjirō Yoshikawa was a sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and later headed Toho Gakkai as board chairman (~1972–1980).

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kōken Unno earned his degrees at Nagoya University. He held positions at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (attested 2002).

Kōshō Uchiyama studied Western philosophy at Waseda University and trained under Kodo Sawaki, whom he succeeded in 1965. Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).
Kōshō Ōtani was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School (~1929–1932) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1932–1935). He was the successor to Kozui Otani.

Lajos Ligeti specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Paris. He taught at Pázmány Péter Catholic University and held the Inner Asian Studies chair at Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Lakshman Joo was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933. He founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

Lakshmi Swaminathan worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938), later becoming a retired lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, earning degrees from Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under G. C. Pande. He held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology. He served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held an attested post at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 1939.

Lama Jabb is a Tibetology scholar. He has served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and as Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology with a PhD from the University of Manchester. He studied under Karma Thinley Rinpoche and Sakya Trizin, and joined the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche studied at Ngor Monastery, where he held the position of Thartse Shabthung in 1959. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers including Yeshe Thubten and the 14th Dalai Lama. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded Kopan Monastery and became spiritual director of the FPMT in 1984.
Lama Tsering Gyaltsen is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.
